metadata.title: ASCO Clinical Practice Guideline for Adjuvant Therapy for Resected Biliary Tract Cancer
metadata.scope: Adjuvant therapy following surgical resection of biliary tract cancer
metadata.disease: Biliary Tract Cancer (Intrahepatic Cholangiocarcinoma, Extrahepatic Cholangiocarcinoma, Gallbladder Cancer)
metadata.target-population: Patients who have undergone resection of biliary tract cancer

clinical-questions.question: Should patients who have undergone surgical resection for biliary tract cancer receive adjuvant chemotherapy?
Should patients who have undergone surgical resection for biliary tract cancer receive adjuvant chemoradiotherapy?

recommendation.statement: Patients who have undergone resection of biliary tract cancer should be offered adjuvant capecitabine chemotherapy for a duration of 6 months

trial.name: BILCAP
trial.population: 447 patients with resected biliary tract cancer
trial.intervention: Capecitabine 1250 mg/m² twice daily, days 1-14, every 3 weeks for 8 cycles (6 months)

subgroup-analysis.subgroup: Benefit observed across all anatomic sites (iCCA, pCCA, dCCA, GBC)
Benefit observed regardless of nodal status
Benefit observed regardless of resection margin status

dose-modifications.modification: Hold until grade ≤1, then reduce by one dose level

qualifying-statements.statement: This recommendation applies to all anatomic subsites of biliary tract cancer
Patients with R0 and R1 resections may benefit
Node-positive and node-negative patients may benefit
Adjuvant therapy should begin within 16 weeks of surgery

recommendation.statement: Patients who have undergone resection of biliary tract cancer with positive surgical margins (R1 resection) may be offered adjuvant chemoradiotherapy with a fluoropyrimidine

trial.name: SWOG S0809
trial.population: 79 patients with extrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma or gallbladder cancer

intervention.phase: Gemcitabine 1000 mg/m² days 1, 8 plus capecitabine 1500 mg/m²/day days 1-14, every 3 weeks for 4 cycles
Capecitabine 1330 mg/m²/day with concurrent radiotherapy (45 Gy in 25 fractions plus boost to 54-59.4 Gy)

radiotherapy-details.dose: 45 Gy in 25 fractions to regional lymphatics
radiotherapy-details.boost: Additional boost to tumour bed (total 50.4-59.4 Gy)

qualifying-statements.statement: Consider for R1 resections, particularly extrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma and gallbladder cancer
Role in intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma less well defined

trial.name: PRODIGE 12-ACCORD 18
trial.population: 196 patients with resected biliary tract cancer
trial.conclusion: GEMOX not recommended as adjuvant therapy

trial.name: Ebata et al
trial.population: 225 patients with resected bile duct cancer
trial.conclusion: Gemcitabine monotherapy not superior to observation

trial.name: JCOG1202 ASCOT
trial.population: 440 patients with resected biliary tract cancer (Japan)
trial.conclusion: S-1 is an alternative adjuvant option, particularly in regions where available

consideration.recommendation: Adjuvant therapy should begin within 16 weeks of surgery once patient has recovered adequately
Both adjuvant chemotherapy and chemoradiotherapy may be considered; multidisciplinary discussion recommended
Adjuvant chemotherapy recommended regardless of nodal status based on BILCAP subgroup analysis
Age alone should not preclude adjuvant therapy; functional status should guide decision-making
Comprehensive genomic profiling should be considered at diagnosis to identify targetable alterations for potential use at recurrence

research-recommendations.recommendation: Further studies needed to evaluate combination adjuvant regimens
Biomarker studies to identify patients most likely to benefit from adjuvant therapy
Studies evaluating adjuvant targeted therapy for patients with actionable mutations

implementation-considerations.consideration: Patient preferences and values should be incorporated into decision-making
Side effect profile of capecitabine should be discussed
Hand-foot syndrome management strategies should be reviewed
Treatment access and cost considerations may be relevant

summary.key-point: Adjuvant capecitabine for 6 months is recommended for patients with resected biliary tract cancer
BILCAP trial demonstrated improved overall survival with capecitabine
Capecitabine dose: 1250 mg/m² twice daily, days 1-14, every 21 days for 8 cycles
Chemoradiotherapy may be considered for R1 resections
S-1 is an acceptable alternative where capecitabine is not available
GEMOX and gemcitabine monotherapy are not recommended as adjuvant therapy
